topic: SAA multi-station decay — spot-check against dome's current (V51.1) WIN-041 text
our_argument_summary: Our review (verdict: Misleading) argues WIN-041 reprocesses the same INTERMAGNET SAA observations already claimed in WIN-004/005/035/037, that multiple stations within the SAA's spatial correlation length are correlated samples of one anomaly (not independent confirmations), that the >=28 nT/yr threshold is a hardcoded model parameter, and that the claim fails the post-hoc test (no monitor.py entry, public data predating registration). The verdict holds, but this spot-check — the first review since 2026-04-07 and the first with the dome's CURRENT WIN-041 text available — found that the dome's page now cites five named stations (TDC, SHE, HER, PST, KOU) with specific rates from 'Direct HAPI pulls 2022-2024' (registered 2026-03-15), plus a new 'boundary-zone decays fastest' dome-vs-globe argument our text does not address. Three of our specific sentences are now factually vulnerable.

The only SAA-decay domain (Domain 8, 'SAA Decay Rate (TTB)') is a single-station entry with predicted=77.0 and observed=77.0 hardcoded to identical values (pass:True, error 0.0%) — a display, not a validation. code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: SAA decay rates and their spatial structure are direct outputs of standard field models (CHAOS-7, WMM secular variation); the mechanism (reversed-flux patches at the CMB) is published (Terra-Nova et al. 2017, Finlay et al. 2020). The dome relabels the cause 'aetheric field separation' while adopting observed values.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: STRENGTHENED this cycle by the dome's own page: WIN-041 is stamped 'Registered: 2026-03-15' with 'Source: Direct HAPI pulls 2022-2024' — the confirming data window ends roughly 15 months BEFORE registration. The dome's own metadata concedes the observation predates the 'prediction'.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The 'aetheric field separation predicts maximum decay at the inter-cell boundary' line on the current page is stated without any derivation — no formula connects dome geometry (H(r)=8537*exp(-r/8619), axially symmetric) to a boundary-zone decay maximum, and an axisymmetric field cannot produce the azimuthal structure the five stations show. The >=28 threshold is a model input (05-model.txt:42).

holes_found.description: Our detail_evidence states the five WINs 'cite overlapping stations and identical time windows.' The dome's current WIN-041 text falsifies this as written: WIN-041 cites five named stations (TDC, SHE, HER, PST, KOU) from 'Direct HAPI pulls 2022-2024', while WIN-004/005 cite CHAOS-7 2000-2025 (a field model, no station list) and WIN-037 cites WMM2025/INTERMAGNET over 2024-2025. The time windows OVERLAP but are not identical, and the other WINs cite no station lists to 'overlap' with. A defender can quote the dome's own source lines to discredit the sentence, and by extension the paragraph. The underlying argument (same network, same regional phenomenon, same secular-variation signal) is correct — the sentence just overclaims.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace 'These WINs cite overlapping stations and identical time windows' with: 'These WINs draw on the same INTERMAGNET observatory network and overlapping multi-year windows of the same secular-variation episode — WIN-004/005 via the CHAOS-7 model (2000-2025), WIN-037 via WMM2025 (2024-2025), WIN-041 via direct station pulls (2022-2024). Different packaging of one regional signal.'

holes_found.description: Our text does not address the dome's strongest current claim in WIN-041: 'Between-cell region (TDC position) decays faster than either cell node — consistent with aetheric field separation at boundary zone... Globe (fluid core) has no mechanism predicting preferential boundary-zone decay.' This dome-vs-globe argument appears on the live page and our entire critique (station non-independence) talks past it. The 'no mechanism' assertion is false — secular-variation spatial structure, including fastest decline in the saddle region during cell separation, is exactly what reversed-flux-patch growth models reproduce (Terra-Nova et al. 2017; Finlay et al. 2020 CHAOS-7 SV maps), and the dome's 'aetheric field separation' boundary-decay 'prediction' has no derivation from the dome's axisymmetric H(r). But a reader comparing our page to theirs will see an unanswered argument.
holes_found.recommendation: Add to detail_verdict_text: 'The dome's newer framing — that the between-cell region (Tristan da Cunha) decays fastest, which the globe allegedly cannot predict — fails twice. First, standard models DO predict the spatial structure of decay: the SAA's deepening and splitting is reproduced by growth of reversed-flux patches at the core-mantle boundary (Terra-Nova et al. 2017), and CHAOS-7 secular-variation maps place the fastest decline precisely in the region between the separating cells. Second, the dome offers no derivation: its field equation H(r)=8537·exp(−r/8619) depends only on radial distance and is azimuthally symmetric — it cannot produce a boundary-zone maximum at all. The five stations' graded rates are evidence for spatially structured core dynamics, not for an aetheric boundary.'

holes_found.description: Internal tension a defender can quote: detail_evidence says 'the dome's own monitoring code hardcodes the validation threshold at >=28 nT/year', while detail_verdict_text says 'no monitor.py entry exists for this value at all — the dome author has not included it in the monitoring suite.' Both are defensible under careful reading (Domain 8 hardcodes the threshold for the single-station TTB check; no domain covers WIN-041's five-station claim) but juxtaposed they read as our review contradicting itself about whether the monitoring code touches this WIN.
holes_found.recommendation: Disambiguate in detail_verdict_text: 'no monitor.py domain covers WIN-041's five-station claim; the only SAA-decay domain (Domain 8) checks a single station (Tsumeb TTB) against a hardcoded predicted=77.0 / observed=77.0 identity — with the 28 nT/yr threshold appearing only in its label string.'

holes_found.description: Our stated spatial correlation length ('~5,000-8,000 km', in detail_verdict_text and tldr_evidence) is undermined by the dome's own station set: computed great-circle distance HER (Hermanus) to KOU (Kourou) is 8,705 km — OUTSIDE our stated upper bound. A defender can use our own number to argue at least one station pair is independent by our own criterion. The correlation-length figure is also uncited.
holes_found.recommendation: Reframe away from a hard threshold: 'All five stations sample the single coherent SAA structure — a feature spanning roughly 100 degrees of longitude whose decay is driven by one reversed-flux-patch system. Correlated samples of one anomaly do not multiply into independent confirmations regardless of pairwise distance; the effective number of independent observations is far closer to one than to five.' Alternatively cite a source for the correlation length and qualify Kourou as a fringe station.

holes_found.description: Our finding (summary row) says 'same INTERMAGNET data as WIN-004/005/035/037'. WIN-004/005 actually cite CHAOS-7, which assimilates observatory data (including INTERMAGNET) plus Swarm satellite data — 'same INTERMAGNET data' is loose. Low risk because the summary row is a simplification, but 'same observational basis' would be unassailable.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional: change finding to '...same observational basis (INTERMAGNET network / CHAOS-7) as WIN-004/005/035/037'.

stronger_arguments.description: The dome's own registration metadata is now the cleanest post-hoc proof: 'Registered: 2026-03-15' with 'Source: Direct HAPI pulls 2022-2024' printed on the same lines of the live page. The confirming data window closed ~15 months before the prediction was registered. No timestamping argument is needed — the dome's own page concedes the sequence. Our detail_verdict_text currently argues post-hoc via 'publicly available at the time of the dome monitor commit', which is weaker than quoting the dome's own dates.

The graded decay rates the dome itself reports (-79.7 boundary, -31.0 fringe) demonstrate azimuthal and latitudinal STRUCTURE in the field's secular variation. The dome's field equation H(r)=8537*exp(-r/8619) is axially symmetric and cannot produce any such structure; standard CMB reversed-flux models do. The dome's own table is evidence against the dome's own geometry — this strengthens the c2 'axisymmetry contradiction' argument with the dome's own numbers.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome's five-station table (/tmp/dome-fetched/02-wins.txt:447-454) reflects real, checkable data: SAA-region observatories genuinely show large negative secular variation, with rates strongest near the anomaly core (TDC -79.7 nT/yr) and weakest at the fringe (KOU -31.0 nT/yr). Citing named stations with rates and a defined window (2022-2024, line 445) is better empirical practice than most dome WINs, and the observation that the between-cell region currently decays fastest is a real feature of the present secular-variation field (consistent with CHAOS-7 SV structure per Finlay et al. 2020).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Three independent failures, each documented in this run's fields: (1) the dome's own page stamps the claim 'Registered: 2026-03-15' against a 2022-2024 data window (post_hoc_evidence above) — observation before 'prediction'; (2) the five stations are correlated samples of one anomaly, so they cannot count as five independent confirmations, and the same regional signal already underwrites WIN-004/005/035/037 (holes_found[0] recommendation); (3) the spatial structure the dome highlights is underivable from its axisymmetric H(r) equation (derives_from_dome_evidence above) while being a standard output of reversed-flux-patch models — the dome's best evidence here is evidence for the standard model.

advocate_mode.best_defense: You concede the decay rates are real physical observations. Your independence objection rests on a '5,000-8,000 km correlation length' — but Hermanus and Kourou are 8,705 km apart by your own criterion, so at minimum two of my stations are independent samples. And I am not merely counting stations: I report a spatial GRADIENT (boundary-zone maximum, -79.7 at TDC falling to -31.0 at the fringe) that I attribute to aetheric field separation at the inter-cell boundary. Your review nowhere rebuts the boundary-zone argument — you respond to a claim ('many stations = many confirmations') that is not the one my current text makes.
advocate_mode.preemptive_recommendation: Apply holes_found[1] and holes_found[3] recommendations together: rebut the boundary-zone argument explicitly (standard SV maps predict the saddle-region maximum; the dome's axisymmetric equation cannot) and reframe the correlation-length sentence so it cannot be turned against us (one coherent anomaly, one driving structure, effective N≈1).

deeper_analysis: This is the first WIN-041 review with the dome's actual V51.1 page text in hand — c1/c2 (April) inferred the WIN's content from V50.6 raw text where it did not appear, and explicitly flagged that uncertainty (c2 code_discrepancies). The inference held up well: verdict, all four code tags, and the core non-independence argument survive contact with the real text. What did not survive: two specific sentences written under inference ('overlapping stations and identical time windows'; the implied absence of ANY monitoring-code touchpoint) and one uncited quantitative bound (correlation length) that the dome's own station geometry now strains. The dome also added a boundary-zone-decay dome-vs-globe argument after our text was written, which we never rebut. None of this threatens the Misleading verdict — the dome's own 'Registered 2026-03-15 / data 2022-2024' stamp makes the post-hoc case stronger than ever — but the page-vs-page comparison is where a defender would attack. Carry-over note: c2 holes_found[1] (axisymmetry contradicts multi-station framing) recommended a text addition that was never integrated and has no open ISS; restated this cycle inside holes_found[1]'s recommendation (the boundary-zone rebuttal subsumes it).
